name: file-upload-streaming-p2
prompt: how can I accept very large file uploads without the server running out of memory

chunks.content: styled the drag-and-drop upload area with a dashed border and a hover highlight
the upload widget shows a progress bar driven by the browser's progress events as bytes are sent
after a photo lands we resize it to a max edge of 2000px for the gallery view
throttle repeated failed logins from the same IP to slow credential stuffing
raised the connection pool ceiling to 40 after seeing checkout timeouts under load
decided to pipe the incoming request body straight to a temp file on disk in fixed-size buffers instead of reading the whole upload into memory
swapped to a streaming multipart parser that emits each part as a readable stream so we never buffer an entire attachment in RAM
for big files we open an S3 multipart upload and forward chunks as they arrive, completing the upload once the last part is flushed
reject any request whose declared content length exceeds the per-plan upload limit before we start reading the body
send a weekly digest email summarizing each team's activity
fixed a memory leak where the request logger held references to completed responses and the heap kept growing
store event times in UTC and render them in the viewer's zone
removed a stale feature flag that had been fully rolled out for months
append every permission change to an immutable audit trail
